newsitem.title: USA: Arco says natives to benefit from Alaska oil field.
newsitem.headline: Arco says natives to benefit from Alaska oil field.

text.p: Developing the newly discovered Alpine oil field will provide significant royalties and employment for Alaska Natives, Arco Alaska Inc. President Ken Thompson said Thursday.
The Atlantic Richfield Co. subsidiary is planning to spend $700 to $800 million on the field, lured by its estimated 250 million to 300 million recoverable barrels of light crude oil.

This investment will benefit Alaska-area natives by earning them royalties -- since they are part owners of the fields -- as well as by winning many of their firms contracts to develop the oil fields, Thompson said in a speech at the Alaska Federation of Natives' annual convention.
The Alpine field, scheduled to start production in 2000, will offer the first commercial oil production from land owned by an Alaska Native corporation.

Most of the Alpine tracts are state-owned, but some are owned by the Barrow-based, Inupiat Eskimo-owned Arctic Slope Regional Corp., one of the 12 regional corporations formed by the 1971 Alaska Native Claims Settlement Act.
Thompson also said the development will "set a new standard that is less costly and has less environmental impact."

To prepare for the development, Arco has spent five years collecting data about the area's fish, wildlife and ecology, and sought advice from residents in Nuiqsut, an Inupiat Eskimo village particularly affected by the development, Thompson said.
"The studies that we have done and the input we received from the village ... has reshaped our development plan," he said.
